theme: Source-backed town-axis register with architectural parts, dating assertions and corrected-location horizons
question: Can the prior Q-1032 measurements, plans, horizons and dates be reconciled without losing their source locators, north references, uncertainty or missingness?
outcome: A 34-town register preserves 1,380 measurement records, 118 dated-part assertions, 620 radiocarbon assertions and 539 source-use records including 46 new DEM tiles. Two exploratory Surkotada wall picks are -11.83 and -11.60 degrees with roughly 5-degree digitizing errors and unknown total error. Thirty-five Wanzke published rows were entered with gon and north distinctions. Corrected Surkotada and Farmana horizons raise usable modern-location profile coverage from 18 to 20 towns. The record audit checks 207 input hashes and 3,009 references. No new radiocarbon determination, inscribed object, scientific orientation statistic or credence update.
challenge: Prior compilations use different schemas, repeat samples and source images, mix architectural parts, and include superseded site coordinates. Lothal imagery values disagree, registration validation failed, and most wall-to-construction-boundary joins remain unresolved.
remedy: Keep each source assertion with a hash and JSON Pointer; label north, dependence, coordinate quality and reported versus partial errors; preserve failed build run-v1; retain all earlier endpoints; compute corrected-location profiles with the unchanged sampler and store acquired tiles on D:.
retry_when: Add surveyed true-north wall bearings, georeferenced plans with new control evidence, phase-linked construction samples or verified site identities. Do not refit the star test on the same examined observations or treat repeated readings as independent imagery.
